question: Who was the President of the Board of Trade when the Cabinet Mission visited India ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Stafford Cripps**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Stafford Cripps** was a British Labour politician and a key member of the Cabinet during World War II.
 
• He was appointed as the President of the Board of Trade in 1945 under Prime Minister Clement Attlee's government.
 
• Stafford Cripps played a significant role in the **Cabinet Mission** that visited India in 1946 to discuss the transfer of power from British rule to Indian leadership.
 
• As a member of the Cabinet Mission, Cripps was instrumental in presenting proposals for the formation of a constituent assembly and an interim government in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cabinet Mission**

 
 
• The Cabinet Mission was a high-powered delegation sent by the British government to India in March 1946.
 
• The mission comprised three members: **Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, and AV Alexander**.
 
• The primary objective was to discuss and plan the transfer of power from British rule to Indian leadership while maintaining India's unity.
 
• The mission proposed a three-tier federal structure and recommended the formation of an interim government and a constituent assembly.
 
• Despite its efforts, the mission failed to achieve a consensus between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League, leading to the eventual partition of India and Pakistan in 1947.
 
 
 
• **Lord Wavell**
 
 
• Lord Wavell was the Viceroy of India from 1943 to 1947.
 
• He played a crucial role in World War II, particularly in the Burma Campaign against Japanese forces.
 
• Wavell initiated the **Wavell Plan** in 1945, which aimed to involve Indian leaders in the governance process through the formation of an Executive Council.
 
• However, the plan was not successful due to disagreements between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.
 
 
 
• **AV Alexander**
 
 
• Albert Victor Alexander, commonly known as AV Alexander, was a British Labour politician and a member of the Cabinet Mission.
 
• He served as the First Lord of the Admiralty during World War II and played a key role in the British war effort.
 
• Alexander was known for his strong support for the Indian independence movement.
 
 
 
• **Pethick Lawrence**
 
 
• Frederick Pethick-Lawrence, 1st Baron Pethick-Lawrence, was a British Labour politician and a member of the Cabinet Mission.
 
• He served as the Secretary of State for India and Burma from 1945 to 1947.
 
• Pethick-Lawrence was a strong advocate for Indian self-governance and played a significant role in the discussions leading to India's independence.
